source.title: LLaTTE: Scaling Laws for Multi-Stage Sequence Modeling in Large-Scale Ads Recommendation
source.authors: Lee Xiong; Zhi-Rong Chen; Rahul Mayuranath; S. Qiu; A. Ozdemir; Lu Li; Yang Hu; David Li; Jing-Tao Ren; Howard Cheng; Fabian Souto Herrera; A. Agiza; Allen Lin; Baruch Epstein; A. Aggarwal; Julia Ulziisaikhan; Chao Wang; D. Ramasamy; Parshva Doshi; Sriman Reddy; Arnold Overwijk

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests scaling behavior in production recommendation models and refines the analogy to language-model scaling: it reports that scaling depends on semantic content, width, and the axis being scaled.
record.gate_note: The study measures NE in recommendation models, not held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy. Its recommendation scaling experiments and cross-stage transfer results bear on V5, V6, and V7. It does not validate predictions from small runs on runs orders of magnitude larger, nor establish the parameter/token allocation power laws in V3. The attention-distribution analyses are not rows because they do not measure a scaling result.
record.test_reason: The study fits log-linear NE-vs-compute scaling curves for transformer sequence models in production ads recommendation, a new setting. This bears on V5 (does the scaling form carry over?) and V7 (slopes depend on axis, content, compute accounting and stage). Upstream-to-ranker transfer at matched compute bears weakly on V6. There are no language-model loss sweeps, no extrapolation tests, no parameter/token allocation optima, and no fixed-parameter shape comparison. T3 fits better than T5: the paper extends the claim to a new setting rather than arguing a version is wrong.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but incomplete. The authors conclude that recommendation sequence models show predictable log-linear (which they call power-law) NE-vs-compute scaling, with sequence length the steepest axis. Semantic content features are a prerequisite that steepens the curves, and sufficient width must precede depth scaling. Upstream gains transfer to the online ranker at ≈50%, and deployment gave ≈0.25% NE reduction and a 4.3% conversion uplift.
record.recipe_differences: This is a production ads-recommendation sequence-model study, using NE rather than held-out language-model cross-entropy and varying depth, width, sequence length, and feature richness rather than language-model parameter, token, and compute sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported scaling behavior varies with content richness, width and depth allocation, sequence length, and whether compute is measured for the full model or only the sequence module; upstream and downstream settings also differ.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed T=400, depth/width allocation strongly changes NE gain. A wide-shallow model with 6.93M parameters (−0.08%) is worse than a deep-balanced one with 2.33M (−0.17%). Near-equal-FLOP narrow vs balanced configurations give −0.10% vs −0.14%. Meanwhile, at matched ~12 GFLOPs, depth-vs-length allocation barely matters (−0.14% vs −0.13%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In recommendation sequence models, shape matters beyond parameter count when width is below a threshold (d≈256), but allocation between depth and length matters little at fixed compute.

record.problems: Experiments use proprietary production data and NE rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy. The paper does not report uncertainty estimates for the scaling results, and some plotted sequence-length results lack numerical values in the text. The fitted curves are not tested as small-run predictions of much larger runs.

untested.parts: No language-model held-out pretraining loss sweeps.
No small-run fit used to predict much larger runs.
No parameter/token optima as powers of compute.
No fixed-parameter-count shape comparison. Table 1 varies parameters and FLOPs together.
Image/video, repeated data and fine-tuning are not tested. The fit is log-linear in ΔNE over ~1.5 compute decades; power-law form over several orders of magnitude is not established.
No downstream benchmarks, and no downstream metric tracked across multiple upstream scales.
No comparison of fitting methods or training schedules.

missing.what: Compute range and number of points behind the Figure 4 fits (axis spans roughly 2e19 to 6e20 FLOPs, ~1.5 decades); no goodness of fit reported
L=8 sequence-length curve stated as run but not shown

record.verdict_notes: Figure 4's α values exactly match Table 3a's downstream-vs-total-FLOPs slopes, yet Section 6 attributes them to upstream experiments on sequence FLOPs: likely mislabeling in the paper. ΔNE values are tiny (0.02% is called significant), and no uncertainty is reported. The 25–30% typical transfer figure is asserted, not measured.

versions.untested_parts: No language-model held-out pretraining loss sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute.
The study fits scaling curves but does not report small-run fits predicting much larger runs.
It compares architecture allocations, including matched-compute configurations, but does not establish parameter-count and token-count optima as stable powers of compute.
No fixed-parameter-count comparison isolating depth, width, or other architecture details.

Tests sequence-model scaling in ads recommendation, including content features; does not test image or video model scaling as such, repeated-data training, fine-tuning, or transfer across other modalities and regimes.
Tests transfer from upstream user models to online ads ranking; does not test general downstream benchmarks or predictability from pretraining loss.

Tests sensitivity to input content, model width/depth, sequence length, and upstream/downstream setting; does not compare alternative fitting methods, parameter-count conventions, or training schedules.

relationships.condition: LLaTTE sequence modules with content features, scaled in depth, width and sequence length (upstream and downstream)
relationships.reason: NE improves monotonically with T and gives positive log-linear slopes per axis (r5–r7, r15, r17–r24, r26–r30).
relationships.display_finding: NE improved monotonically with T, with positive log-linear slopes across depth, width and sequence length.

relationships.reason: Without content, depth scaling gives a minor gain and the slope is shallow (α=−0.082); the authors call content a prerequisite (r13, r16).
relationships.display_finding: Depth scaling produced only minor gains with exponent −0.082, leading the authors to identify semantic content as a prerequisite.

relationships.reason: The upstream sequence-length slope is roughly 40–45% of the downstream slope (0.116 vs 0.265 total; 0.094 vs 0.238 sequence-only) (r25, r31).
relationships.display_finding: Upstream sequence-length slopes were roughly 40–45% of downstream slopes: 0.116 versus 0.265 overall and 0.094 versus 0.238 for sequence-only scaling.

relationships.condition: Two matched-compute (~12 GFLOPs) upstream configurations transferred to the online ranker
relationships.reason: Upstream gains of −0.14% and −0.13% both give −0.07% downstream, τ≈50–53% (r32–r37). There are only two points at one compute level.
relationships.display_finding: Upstream changes of −0.14% and −0.13% both transferred as −0.07% downstream, giving τ≈50–53% across two configurations at one compute level.

relationships.condition: Scaling axis, content richness, compute accounting, and upstream vs downstream stage
relationships.reason: Slopes range 0.082–0.265 by axis and content (r16–r19). Depth α is 0.200 vs 0.106 under total vs sequence FLOPs (r20, r26). Depth's T-slope varies (r6), and content changes depth gain (r13, r15).
relationships.display_finding: Slopes ranged from 0.082 to 0.265 by axis and content; depth α was 0.200 under total FLOPs versus 0.106 under sequence FLOPs, while depth's token-scaling slope and gains also varied.
